title: OFD identity allegedly lost across dup2/exec
mechanism: Rejected claim: a captured file operation or deferred close cleanup could resolve a reused descriptor number to a different open file description after close/dup2, or exec CLOEXEC cutover could close the wrong object. Source keeps the Arc captured (get_file_fast!, dup_exact, ClosedFile) and exec closes CLOEXEC entries of a private table after other threads exit.
contract: dup2(2)/close(2)/execve(2): an in-flight call keeps the OFD it started with, dup2 installs the source OFD, and exec closes only FD_CLOEXEC descriptors.
observed: Identity is preserved: a blocked read returned the original pipe's byte in 32/32 samples, dup2 replacement and CLOEXEC exec cutover behaved as on Linux (test PASS on Asterinas, SMP=2).

repro.how_to_run: Build statically with pthreads, place at /test/test_bugCR-1_ofd_identity in the guest, and run via run_bugCR-1_ofd_identity.sh. See repro/README.md.
repro.negative_result: Asterinas guest PASS at 4ba4abbe8cb3f2892129d67b0301cf247bbdda0f, SMP=2 (identity preserved)

caveats: The guest serial log was removed with the worktree. The PASS output survives in investigation.md and turn01_A.log only. Small sample, pipes only. Debate did not run. The test's exit status does not fail on raced_new. The recorded counts are the evidence.
